Ren, 18 October 2026, on the direction proposed for the overnight work: "currently i have no problem of heading to your direction. I think you also sees it, good job, please continue" ([source](../../../../../../sources/15-codex-theory-conversations/2026-10-18-representation-scope-go.md)). The direction is the AI's proposal, and this section is accountable to the work, not to that message.

**The question.** Every `World`, `Flow` and `Web` is indexed by one sequence of natural-number steps shared by all relata (chapter block A, "Discrete steps, one shared index"). `Becoming.Order` and `Becoming.OrderNormal` showed, for a world given with that index, that the laws use only the partial order of joined exchanges (study §102). The opposite direction stayed open in §8.2: starting from relations, is there a shared index, how much of it do the relations fix, and is the rest a commitment of the representation?

**The relational start.** `LocalLaw X E σ` gives exchanges `E` acting on configurations `X → σ` of relata `X`. Each exchange touches some relata (`touches`). It leaves every other relatum's state as it was (`keeps`), and it changes a relatum it touches as the states of the relata it touches determine (`reads`). Nothing gives a global step. What each relatum undergoes is its own course: the exchanges touching it, in order (`ownCourse`). A shared index is an interleaving: a list of exchanges whose own course at every relatum is the given one (`Interleaves`). The exchange process `LocalLaw.process` is a `Generative.Process`, so its traces are traces of the base.

**What is proved** (`Becoming.Interleavings`).
- **Exchanges sharing no relatum commute** (`act_comm`). An exchange moves forward past exchanges sharing no relatum with it without changing the configuration (`run_move`).
- **Equal own courses, equal configurations.** With the relata listed, two lists giving every relatum the same own course reach the same configuration from the same start (`run_of_courses`), and so do two traces of the exchange process (`trace_of_courses`). In particular, two traces interleaving the same courses end alike (`trace_of_interleavings`), and two exchanges sharing no relatum end alike in either order (`trace_swap`). The proof splits the second list at the first exchange sharing a relatum with the head of the first (`split_heads`), shows that it is that head (the own courses at a shared relatum begin with it), and moves it forward.
- **The index is built.** With exchanges told apart, a scheduler takes an exchange that heads the remaining course of every relatum it touches (`ready`, `pick`) and drops it from those courses (`pop`). Where some interleaving exists, every ready exchange can be taken first (`pop_interleaves`), so the scheduler is never stuck. Each stage removes at least one exchange from the courses, so it completes within as many stages as the courses have exchanges in all (`total_pop`, `schedule_some`). What it returns is an interleaving (`schedule_interleaves`). So an interleaving exists exactly where the scheduler completes (`schedule_iff`), that is, exactly where some trace of the exchange process takes every relatum through its given course (`traced_iff`).
- **Where the courses fix the index.** With the relata listed, equal own courses force equal lists exactly where every exchange touches some relatum and every two exchanges are the same or share a relatum (`unique_iff`; on the traces from any configuration, `traced_unique_iff`). Where two exchanges share no relatum, the two orders have the same own courses (`swap_courses`). Where an exchange touches nothing, the list with it and the list without it have the same own courses.

**Reading (the AI's, pending Ren).** The shared index of steps is a reading of the relations, not their ground. What each relatum undergoes, and in what order, is its own course. A global index adds only an order between exchanges that share no relatum (and the placing of exchanges that touch nothing), and that order changes no configuration. Where every two exchanges share a relatum, the index is derived from the relations. Elsewhere it is a commitment of the representation: a choice among the interleavings that the relations leave open and that the configurations do not read. This answers the formal half of the §8.2 item for finite courses of a local law. It does not answer whether every becoming has such a local law (the warrant question of §8.5 stays open). It also does not touch the other identification in block A, of conditions with relata.

**Relation to the order results.** `Becoming.Order` starts from a world with an index and a supplied footprint, and shows that renumberings keeping the order of joined exchanges keep every premise. This module starts from the courses and builds the index. The AI expects them to meet in content, though this is not proved here: for a world, a renumbering would keep the order of joined exchanges exactly where it keeps every relatum's own course. They are not joined by definition, because `Becoming.Order` takes a footprint over a world's steps while `LocalLaw` takes one per exchange. A correspondence theorem is left open (it is not needed for either result).

**Self-review.** The statements were read against the Lean.
- `run_of_courses` and `unique_iff` need the relata listed (`∀ x, x ∈ xs`). That is how "every relatum" becomes a finite test (`shares`) without deciding anything about `X` beyond the list. The scheduler needs `DecidableEq E` and nothing else.
- `reads` asks that an exchange's effect on a relatum it touches depend only on the relata it touches. A law in which an exchange reads a relatum it does not change is represented by letting it touch that relatum and keep its state. The courses then include reads as well as changes. A finer law with separate read and write footprints would let reads of one relatum commute, and is not treated.
- The uniqueness equivalence is exact in both directions. The backward direction uses only that the heads of two lists with the same own courses meet at a relatum shared by both. The forward direction builds the two-element counterexample `[e, f]`, `[f, e]` from any pair sharing no listed relatum, and `[e]`, `[]` from an exchange touching nothing.
- No `propext`, `Quot.sound` or `Classical.choice` occurs. `decide` appears only in `ready.heads`, on the supplied `DecidableEq E`. The module compiles from the prelude with `Becoming.Frame` (scratch build: `unclean` empty, `with_axioms` empty).
